title: astra.registry.migration-notice/1
description:
log/migration-notice-<n>.json — MIG-13's marker, one per round (contract B.4; MIG-13; MIG-14; ROLL-32; registry plan ROLL-63). It is committed by hand with each round's sends (registry plan M-T5.3; reg.92 writes round 1 at R4b, reg.99 round 2), and nothing generates it.

WHO READS IT, which is why it has a schema at all: tools/validate.mjs, the first of the checks the publish path runs, judges every marker on the tree against this file, loaded from THIS repository and never from the tree under test; tools/cutover-preflight.mjs, ROLL-32's gate, judges the markers on a ref against this file read from the same ref, the way it judges policy/binding-deadline.json; the plugins service, for the listing banner MIG-13 tells to read the round and the announced date from the marker; and registry plan M-T5.4's deadline watch once it is built. Until contract 0.31.0 none of the four had a published statement of what a marker's members ARE — B.4 listed them and typed none — so each reader typed them for itself, and the one reader in this repository that asked, the preflight, withheld rather than guess (dev/couplings.md entry 58).

THE TYPES ARE B.4's, AND ONLY B.4's. Contract 0.31.0 states them on the page first: `schema` the string below; `round` a JSON integer of at least 1 and at most 4294967295, the MIG-13 round the marker records, written as an integer with no fraction part and no exponent, never a string, a fraction or null; `sent_at` and `cutover_planned_at` §0.7 times that name a real UTC instant, with no seconds field of 60. A schema asserting `integer` while the page said nothing would have been a file outrunning its source, which is the wrong direction under SCOPE-1, and it is why this file did not exist before that version.

`round` IS AN INTEGER BECAUSE THE CONDITION IS. The token file publishes `cutover_planned_at` as `conditional` with `{"iff": {"round": {"not": [1]}}}`, which names the integer `1`, and every reader compares without coercion. A marker spelling its round `"1"` makes that condition take its other branch: a conforming round-1 marker is then required to carry a date it cannot have, at the gate that decides whether the catalogue may move, and the refusal points at whoever wrote the marker.

A CEILING ON `round`, AND IT IS NOT MIG-13's. The plugins service's reader holds a round in 32 unsigned bits and refuses 4294967296 — measured by that session, running it — so B.4 publishes `maximum` 4294967295: a reader's private ceiling is exactly the divergence a published type exists to close. MIG-13 has three rounds, so nothing is lost; and the ceiling is the reader's, not a copy of MIG-13's round count, which nothing here would compare with the page.

THE LITERAL, WHICH NO JSON SCHEMA CAN STATE. B.4 says `round` is "written as an integer with no fraction part and no exponent (`1`, never `1.0` or `1e0`)". `type: integer` is a property of the VALUE, and `1.0`, `1e0` and `1E0` are the value 1, so this file admits them and a JavaScript validator cannot tell them from `1` once the text is parsed — while the service's reader, which asks the literal for an unsigned integer, refuses them (measured the same way). So tools/validate.mjs and the cutover preflight read the member's RAW TEXT with tools/lib/json-literal.mjs, which also refuses a second `round` member (JSON.parse keeps the last one, so a duplicate is a value no two readers need agree on).

EXACTLY FOUR MEMBERS, and `$comment` is NOT among them, for the reason schema/deadline-v1.json gives at length: B.4 fixes the member set with the word "exactly", this record crosses a party boundary, and a member one party admits and another refuses is a two-way-test failure (§0.8) found by whichever side guessed wrong. This file constrains the WRITER; a reader ignoring an unknown member is SCOPE-3's rule and is not contradicted by it.

THE CONDITION, WRITTEN AS `oneOf` BECAUSE tools/lib/jsonschema.mjs IMPLEMENTS NO `if`. The two branches mirror the token file's predicate exactly, value for value: `round` is `1` and the date is absent; `round` is not `1` and the date is present. A round-1 marker carrying the date matches neither, which is MIG-14's "never in a marker before it"; a round-2 marker without it matches neither, which is B.4's "from round 2". tools/selftest/migration-notice.mjs holds the two statements of the condition to one another over every round it can name, so this file and the token file cannot drift apart in silence.

WHOLE SECONDS, AND `Z` (§0.7), NAMING A REAL UTC INSTANT, AND NEVER SECOND 60 (B.4, for these two members only). The pattern bounds each field — month 01–12, day 01–31, hour 00–23, minute and second 00–59 — so an hour of 24 and a second of 60 are refused here. It cannot tell a real day from `2026-02-30`, so tools/validate.mjs and the preflight round-trip each value through `Date` and compare the ISO string, which refuses all three. `2026-02-30` and hour 24 are not RFC 3339 date-times in the first place (RFC 3339 §5.6 and §5.7); refusing second 60, which RFC 3339 permits in a leap-second month, is the one place B.4 departs from it, and it does so for these two members and for no other §0.7 time. A §0.7 DATE (`YYYY-MM-DD`) is refused: §0.7 reserves that format for `added_at` and `verified_at`, so MIG-13's "its date" and "the announced cutover date" are moments on the wire.

WHAT NOTHING HERE CAN CHECK: how `round` is written (tools/lib/json-literal.mjs does, above); whether a day exists (the round trip does); that the file's `<n>` is its `round` (the preflight refuses a disagreement, and no published sentence states it), that there is one marker per round, and that no marker announces a superseded date (MIG-13, n28). Those are facts about several files, and they are the preflight's and M-T5.4's.

round.$comment: B.4 from contract 0.31.0: a JSON integer of at least 1 and at most 4294967295, the MIG-13 round this marker records. `type: integer` refuses "1", 1.5 and null; `minimum: 1` refuses 0 and every negative; `maximum` is the plugins service's 32-bit ceiling, published. The literal form (`1`, never `1.0` or `1e0`) is not expressible here and is checked on the raw text — see the description.

sent_at.$comment: The moment this round was sent — MIG-13's "its date" — naming a real UTC instant, never second 60. ROLL-32's 30 days and registry plan ROLL-63's alarms count from it and never from the commit, so a re-send that re-commits a marker with a later cutover date keeps this value (MIG-13; n10).

cutover_planned_at.$comment: The announced cutover moment, naming a real UTC instant and never second 60, carried exactly where `round` is not 1 — see the `oneOf` below. ROLL-32 holds cutover until it has come.

oneOf.$comment: Round 1: the marker committed once, at R4b, before any cutover date exists. It carries no `cutover_planned_at` (B.4: "from round 2"; MIG-14: "never in a marker before it").

Every other round: the date is required. Written as `not const 1` rather than `minimum: 2`, so that it is the token file's `{"not": [1]}` in this file's words and not a second rule that happens to agree with it on today's rounds.
